text:
Maria G: heads-up: acme-corp reports SSO started failing after their IdP maintenance window. Users see 'Assertion signature invalid' and 403 at our ACS.
Tom B: can you paste the IdP metadata URL and the ACS value they set on their side? small mismatch issues often are just a slash or an encoded char.
Maria G: idp metadata: https://idp.acme.example/saml/metadata.xml
Maria G: ACS configured: https://app.redwood.example/sso/callback/acs
Cheng Li: I pulled our metadata-watcher trace. During their rotation our poller got a 429 and respected Retry-After; watcher extended the stale TTL and kept the old keyset for ~8m.
Cheng Li: watcher log snippet:
```
2026-03-16T09:27:14Z WARN metadata-watcher GET https://idp.acme.example/saml/metadata.xml -> 429 Retry-After: 300
2026-03-16T09:27:14Z INFO metadata-watcher stale-ttl extended to 8m
2026-03-16T09:35:10Z ERROR sso-verify assertion signature failed thumbprint mismatch expected: 03:7A:... got: F2:9C:...
```
Sara (Support): customer says desktop+mobile both blocked. A handful of users see a 400 missing relaystate error, but majority are 403. They've escalated to their IdP ops who confirm they rotated signing keys ~09:30 UTC.
Tom B: do they have multiple <KeyDescriptor use="signing"> entries in metadata? key order can change during rotation.
Maria G: yes, new metadata includes two signing keys and the order is different from previous version. They also host metadata via a rate-limited endpoint.
Cheng Li: current behavior: if a fetch fails (429) we keep serving last-good metadata for a backoff window. Our verifier picks the first signing key when no KeyInfo matches the assertion. With order swapped + stale metadata we attempted verification against the wrong key. Failure surfacing as 'Assertion signature invalid'.
Tom B: root cause looks like a race: IdP rotated keys and our poller got throttled, leaving our tenant with stale keyset. Also our verifier didn't try to re-fetch on signature failure.
Sara (Support): customer is blocked. What's a safe short-term workaround?
Cheng Li: short-term options:
- Accept metadata upload from IdP ops/support and attach it to tenant record manually (fast, manual).
- Implement on-demand fetch+retry if verification fails (safer).
- Temporarily relax key-order assumption and try verifying against all signing keys present in cached metadata (moderately safe).
Tom B: I'm going to ship an emergency patch that does an immediate on-demand metadata fetch when signature verification fails, skipping the backoff if Retry-After is present. If fetch returns 200 and keyset changed, we retry verification. This keeps attack surface small.
Tom B: will canary in ~30–40m, then roll if green.
Maria G: told the customer we can accept a metadata XML upload as fallback; they prefer quick fix from us instead. They've uploaded the XML to the secure ticket attachment.
Cheng Li: opened INF-5248 and attached poller logs, failure traces, and timeline. CC @oncall-sre for rollout watch.
oncall-sre: noted. monitor canary and be ready to revert the on-demand behavior if we see spikes or odd metadata responses. Add alerting for metadata keyset churn.
Tom B: canary deployed at 09:50 UTC. Observed a successful on-demand fetch for tenant-acme and subsequent successful assertion verification in canary logs.
Tom B: rolling to prod now. Will keep 15m watch; add extra logging for 'metadata-source' and 'key-thumbprint-used'.
Cheng Li: follow-ups post-deploy:
- reduce aggressive stale-ttl extension when receiving 429; prefer exponential reattempts up to a cap.
- emit telemetry event when a tenant's metadata keyset changes and when verification had to trigger on-demand fetch.
- update runbook with steps for handling IdP rate-limiting during rotations (include manual upload flow).
Maria G: customer reports 90% of users can sign in again after prod roll. A few legacy browsers still hit relaystate issues; support triaging separately.
Sara (Support): marking the escalation for monitored close; will reopen if we see re-occurrence. Saved runbook snippet and INF-5248 notes in ticket.
Tom B: will follow up tomorrow with an RCA and proposed longer-term fixes (e.g., 1) warm-key fetching, 2) better keyinfo matching heuristics, 3) idp-side guidance for ramping rotation traffic).
Maria G: thanks all — file conversation into INF-5248 and link to runbook.
